title: Hadith Qudsi on Divine Justice and Mercy
summary: This Hadith Qudsi emphasizes Allah's prohibition of injustice and His provision for guidance, sustenance, forgiveness, and more.
translation: Hadith narrated by Abu Dhar Al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), stating that Allah Almighty said: "O My servants, I have prohibited injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me and I shall guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me and I shall feed you. O My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me and I shall clothe you. O My servants, you sin by day and night, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I shall forgive you. O My servants, you will not be able to harm Me or benefit Me. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart among you, it would not increase My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart among you, it would not decrease My kingdom in anything. O My servants, if your first and last, and human and jinn, were to stand in one field and ask of Me, and I were to give every one whatever he asked for, that would not decrease what I have any more than a needle decreases the sea if put into it. O My servants, indeed it is but your deeds that I account for you and then recompense you for, so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah. And whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself."
